# Hypothesis

H1: Individualistic attitudes (DV) will be stronger among full-time employed individuals than among unemployed individuals (IV).

H2:Gender-equality attitudes (DV) will be associated with daily time spent enhancing appearance (IV).

```{r load packages}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrain)
```

# Load the processed data 

```{r Load data}
#Load the processed data 
h1data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h1_revised.csv")
h2data <- read.csv("data/processed_data/h2_revised.csv")
```

#Check Kind of Data to make decision about plot

```{r Check Data and Types of Variables }
str(h1data)
str(h2data)
```

## H1 

### H1: Boxplot
```{r Boxplot}
#Basic Layout, labeling axes and title, and using fill = to have different boxes for the different categories of the x -axis, Employment Group variable
h1BoxPlot <- ggplot(data = h1data,
                aes(x= Employment_group,
                    y = ind_rev_mean,
                    fill = Employment_group)) +
  labs(x = "Employment Status",
       y = "Individualistic Attitudes",
       title = "Individualistic Attitudes Compared by Employment Status")
h1BoxPlot


# Replace automatic x-axis tick labels with self picked Labels 
h1BoxPlot <- h1BoxPlot + scale_x_discrete(labels = (c("Full Time", "Unemployed")))
h1BoxPlot

# Add more precise scaling to the y axis using scale_y_continuous
h1BoxPlot <- h1BoxPlot +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(1,7),
    breaks = 1:7)

#Set the text size using base_size = inside theme_gray()
h1BoxPlot <- h1BoxPlot + theme_gray(base_size=13)
h1BoxPlot


#No need to add subgroups with fill = 


# Add the actual plot type (Boxplot) using geom_boxplot()
h1BoxPlot <- h1BoxPlot + geom_boxplot()
h1BoxPlot


#Add error bars representing 95% CI using the mean_cl_boot option in stat_summary and geom = "errorbar"
h1BoxPlot <- h1BoxPlot + stat_summary (fun.data = "mean_cl_boot",
                                       geom = "errorbar",
                                       position = "dodge")
h1BoxPlot


#Observation: The mean and IQR of the two Emloyment Groups are neaarly identical. There seems to be no mean difference
```

### H1: Violin Plot (+ Boxplot)

```{r Violin Plot}
h1ViolinPlot <- ggplot (data = h1data,
                        aes(x = Employment_group,
                            y = ind_rev_mean,
                            fill = Employment_group)) + 
  labs(x = "Employment Status",
       y = "Individualistic Attitudes",
       fill = "Employment Group",
       title = "Individualistic Attitudes by Employment Status") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels=(c("Full Time", "Unemployed"))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1,7),
                     breaks = 1:7) +
  theme_gray(base_size = 14) +
  geom_violin(position = "dodge") +
  geom_boxplot(position = "dodge",
               width = 0.2) +
stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_cl_boot",
               geom = "errorbar",
               position = "dodge")
h1ViolinPlot

# Observation: The distributions for Full Time and Unemployed look very similar 
```

### H1: Raincloud (+Violin and Boxplot)

```{r Rainplot}
h1RainPlot <- ggplot (data = h1data,
                        aes(x = Employment_group,
                            y = ind_rev_mean,
                            fill = Employment_group)) + 
  labs(x = "Employment Status",
       y = "Individualistic Attitudes",
       title = "Individualistic Attitudes by Employment Status") +
  scale_x_discrete(labels=(c("Full Time", "Unemployed"))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(1,7),
                     breaks = 1:7) +
  theme_gray(base_size = 14) +
  geom_rain(alpha = .5) +
   geom_jitter(width = .05,
               alpha = 0.1,
               size =.005,
               height = 0.3)
h1RainPlot

#adjusting the individual scatterplots of the rainplot using geom_jitter, where: width = is how much points are spread out horizontally; alpha = the transparancy of points with 0 being invisible; size = the size of the individual points; and height = how far points are spread horizontally
```

## H2

### H2: Scatterplot + Regressionline 

```{r Scatterplot}
h2Scatterplot <- ggplot(data = h2data,
                        aes(x = Gender_Equality_mean,
                            y = appearance_time_sum)) +
  labs(x = "Gender equality attitude scores",
       y = "Total time spent on Appearance",
       title = "Relationship of Gender Equality Attitudes and Time Spent on Appeance") +
  scale_x_continuous( limits = c(0,8),
                      breaks = 1:7) +
  scale_y_continuous( limits = c(0,1500),
                      breaks = seq(0,1500, by = 240)) +
  theme_gray(base_size = 14) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_jitter( width = 0.1,
               height = 0,
               alpha = 0.2,
               size = 1) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")
h2Scatterplot
```

### H2: Jitter + Regressionline
```{r Jitterplot}
h2JitterLinePlot <- ggplot(data = h2data,
                    aes(x=Gender_Equality_mean,
                        y=appearance_time_sum))+
    geom_jitter(width = .12,height=.04,alpha=.04,size = .6)+
    labs(x="Gender Equality Attitude Score",
       y="Total Time Spent on Appearance",
       title="Relationship between Gender Equality Attitudes and Time Spent on Appearance") +
  theme_gray(base_size = 18) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

h2JitterLinePlot
```

## Save figures
Run after creating the plots. Save PNG files in the project's figures folder.
```{r}

#Create figure folder 
dir.create("figures",showWarnings=FALSE)

#Save figures
ggsave("figures/h1ViolinPlot.png",plot=h1ViolinPlot,width=10,height=6,dpi=300)
ggsave("figures/h2JitterLinePlot.png",plot=h2JitterLinePlot,width=10,height=6,dpi=300)

#To save another plot, change the filename and plot object (e.g., h1Viol or h1Rain).
```
